current_price_note: STALE / effectively untradeable. Yahoo Finance's regularMarketTime for the last real trade in IPR.NZ was 2025-10-23 (regularMarketPrice 0.003); the monthly price series has printed an unchanged $0.003 in every month since December 2023, i.e. this is a stale last-print sitting at (or one tick above) the NZX minimum-tick region, not a market-clearing price discovered through actual trading. Free float is ~14% (Chang Ku Ee 77.4% + KYCZ Ltd 8.6%), so a per-share intrinsic-value comparison against this print is nearly meaningless in liquidity terms -- there is effectively no market to sell into at any price. Upside/downside is still computed below so the cross-ticker screener functions, but should be read as 'the current quote is not a reliable transaction price', not as a tradeable mispricing.
model_note: IPR.NZ (Iperion Limited) is NOT a growth-DCF candidate. Iperion has never earned a dollar of revenue in any period on record -- FY2019 through FY2026, roughly seven audited years, all show $0 revenue. Every year's free cash flow is negative (FY2026: -$269,849; FY2025: -$447,900; FY2024: -$734,204), funded entirely by shareholder capital and, most recently, related-party loans. There is no growth rate to compound, no repeatable margin to project, and no terminal value to capitalise -- a Gordon-growth or component-built FCF DCF applied to a structurally negative, non-existent cash-flow stream produces a meaningless (and typically hugely negative, i.e. nonsensical) number. This model instead follows the AFC.NZ / BGI.NZ precedent in this repository: a probability-weighted mix of (a) insolvency / wind-up (bear), (b) persistence as a going-concern shell valued at net tangible assets plus a modest NZX-listing option value (base), and (c) a bottom-up, heavily-diluted, heavily-discounted Pathoglaze commercialisation scenario (bull).

inputs.net_debt_note: No debt on the FY2026 balance sheet (TotalDebt = 0). Net debt shown here as negative (i.e. net CASH of $155,492) purely for schema completeness; it is NOT subtracted from or added to the scenario valuations below because those are built directly off reported shareholders' equity (which already nets cash against all liabilities), not off an enterprise-value bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column is 0 for every period FY2019-FY2026; no share-based payment expense has ever been disclosed. No SBC adjustment required (owner FCF = reported FCF = -$269,849 FY2026).
inputs.shares_growth_note: Shares outstanding (514,894,500) have been unchanged for at least 7 years -- no dilution to date. Held flat in the base and bear scenarios; the bull scenario explicitly models a one-off dilutive capital raise as a separate mechanic (see assumptions.bull), not as a continuous SBC-style drift, because it is a discrete, disclosed financing event (Elitesoft Asia facility expansion / equity raise), not gradual share-based compensation.
inputs.units: absolute dollars (not thousands or millions) except shares_outstanding, which is in millions per Metrics.csv convention
inputs.audit_opinion_note: Auditor issued a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph in the FY2026 (year ended 31-Mar-2026, signed 30-Jun-2026) audit report. This is a less severe finding than AFC.NZ's/BGI.NZ's disclaimers of opinion (the auditor DID form an opinion, but flagged material uncertainty over the going-concern basis of preparation).
inputs.related_party_facility_note: Elitesoft Asia Sdn Bhd (related to 77.4% shareholder/director Chang Ku Ee) provided a $250,000 unsecured facility at 8% (HKMA Base Rate + 4%), expandable to US$1,000,000 subject to shareholder and NZX approval. Replaced an earlier interest-free $150,000 loan from Mr Ee directly (15-Jun-2026). Mr Ee also gave a 12-month financial support commitment from FY2026 sign-off.
inputs.outsourcing_fee_waiver_note: Three Summit Ventures (outsourced Malaysian manufacturing partner under the Pilot Outsourcing Agreement) has fully waived its normally-fixed $400,000/year facility fee through 31-Mar-2028, meaning forward annual cash burn is admin/listing-cost only (~$295k/yr) rather than the full contracted cost base.
inputs.licence_targets_waived_note: The Pathoglaze licence's own contractual performance targets (customer numbers, SGD$150,000 of sales by September 2026) and the inventor's royalty were PERMANENTLY WAIVED post FY2026 year-end -- removing the only externally-set commercial milestone for the technology and signalling even the closest counterparties do not expect near-term commercial traction on the original timeline.
inputs.ownership_concentration_note: Chang Ku Ee 77.4% + KYCZ Ltd 8.6% = ~86% combined; free float ~14%. The controlling shareholder is simultaneously the company's primary funding lifeline (directly and via the related Elitesoft Asia facility), a material governance and dilution-control risk.

historical_growth.equity_3yr_cagr_note: No true 3-year window is available -- the Metrics.csv annual data has a gap between FY2020 and FY2024 (no FY2021/22/23 annual reports were sourced). The closest available datapoint is the FY2024-to-FY2026 (2-year) equity CAGR of -74.3% (0.814081m to 0.053803m).
historical_growth.equity_5yr_cagr_note: No true 5-year window is available for the same reason. The closest available datapoint is the FY2019-to-FY2026 (7-year) equity CAGR of -41.9% (2.405445m to 0.053803m).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Not applicable in the conventional sense -- there is no revenue to grow (zero in every period FY2019-FY2026) and no positive-earnings base to compound. Shareholders' equity has collapsed at roughly -74%/yr over the most recent 2 available years (FY2024-FY2026) and -42%/yr over the full 7-year span with data (FY2019-FY2026) as accumulated losses ($5,619,053) have eaten through issued capital ($5,672,856), leaving net assets of just $53,803 at FY2026. EPS and FCF CAGRs are null because every year is a loss and the loss trend does not compound meaningfully (losses actually NARROWED in FY2026 -- $294,595 vs $455,683 in FY2025 -- purely because the manufacturing partner waived its fixed fee, not because of any operating improvement).
historical_growth.notes: There is no historical growth to project forward. The single meaningful historical trend is the destruction of book equity: NZ$2.4m (FY2019) to NZ$0.05m (FY2026), a ~98% decline over 7 years, funded entirely by shareholder capital raised at the outset with no revenue ever generated to replace it. Stock-based compensation is nil throughout, so no SBC/dilution adjustment applies -- the entire valuation problem here is going-concern and pre-commercial technology risk, not share-based dilution (that risk is instead modelled explicitly as financing dilution in the bull scenario, see assumptions.bull).

base.narrative: Company persists as a going-concern shell. The controlling shareholder's 12-month support letter and the Elitesoft Asia facility hold, admin-only cash burn (~$295k/yr, since the $400k/yr outsourcing fee is waived through FY2028) continues to be funded by related-party loans/support, and no commercial sale of Pathoglaze occurs within the valuation horizon. Value = FY2026 net tangible assets ($53,803) plus a modest NZX-listing option value reflecting the scarcity of a clean, compliant (if tiny) NZX quotation to a reverse-takeover promoter. This is NOT the post-RTO entity's value -- a shell acquirer issuing new consideration shares to itself means existing IPR holders retain only the pre-money shell claim, not a share of whatever gets injected.
base.shell_scarcity_value_note: Set at the midpoint of a $200k-$400k range, below the AFC.NZ base-case precedent ($500k), reflecting IPR's smaller absolute size, its going-concern paragraph (versus a cleaner opinion at some points in AFC's history), and total dependence on a single controlling shareholder's discretionary, non-binding support for solvency. The range reflects genuine promoter demand for tiny, compliant NZX shells as reverse-listing vehicles (avoiding a full IPO process), balanced against IPR's negligible free float (~14%), thin remaining net asset base, and the fact no MOU or RTO discussion of any kind is currently disclosed (unlike AFC's pre-MOU Fast Track Group discussions) -- so this is pure listing-scarcity value, not transaction-specific option value.
base.burn_note: FY2027-FY2031 admin-only cash burn projection (manufacturing fee waived through FY2028, assumed to resume at a modest level or be re-negotiated thereafter). Funded, base case, by continued related-party loans/support -- consistent with the pattern to date. Shown for schema completeness; NOT subtracted a second time from the tangible-equity valuation, because the funding mechanism (further related-party debt) is a wash against equity as long as shareholder support continues, which is the base case's core assumption. If that assumption fails, that is definitionally the bear case.
base.discounting_note: No perpetuity cash-flow stream exists to discount (burn is a funding wash under the base-case assumption, not a return to equity). A 30% cost-of-equity is disclosed for schema completeness and used only in the entry-price 15%-hurdle comparison context, not to discount a terminal FCF. See wacc_rationale below for the stacked build-up.

bull.narrative: The cocoa/coffee jute-bag trial with the unnamed multinational chocolate manufacturer converts into a first signed long-term commercial supply agreement, followed by modest expansion into adjacent trialled applications (food packaging, textiles). Revenue is modelled as a bottom-up ramp from a small pilot order to a genuine but still-niche run-rate by year 5. This scenario explicitly prices in (a) the 30% commission payable to Three Summit Ventures on gross sales under the Pilot Outsourcing Agreement, (b) a near-certain dilutive equity/debt-conversion raise to fund working-capital and scale-up (modelled as a discrete $750,000 raise at an improved but still speculative $0.006/share, issuing ~125.0m new shares -- a ~19.5% dilution of the existing 514.9m-share base), and (c) a heavy time/execution discount (30% WACC) reflecting that this remains, even in the 'success' branch, an unproven single-product, single-customer-concentrated micro-cap.
bull.revenue_ramp_note: Illustrative 5-year ramp from a first pilot order (Year 1, $50k) to a genuine-but-still-niche run-rate (Year 5, $1.5m) if the chocolate-manufacturer trial converts and 1-2 further customers follow. This remains a small fraction of the addressable antimicrobial-coatings market and is NOT a base-rate expectation -- it is the bull scenario's own internal 'what does success look like' build.
bull.commission_note: 30% commission on gross sales payable to Three Summit Ventures under the Pilot Outsourcing Agreement is embedded in the assumed net margin, not added as a separate deduction on top of the exit multiple.
bull.exit_revenue_multiple_note: A conservative revenue multiple (1.5x) for a newly-commercial, single-product, single-customer-concentrated specialty-chemicals licensor at a genuinely small scale ($1.5m revenue) -- well below multiples paid for established, diversified, profitable specialty-chemicals businesses, reflecting the concentration and technology risk that persists even after a first sale.
bull.dilution_note: A $750,000 raise is assumed necessary to fund working capital and scale-up ahead of/alongside the ramp (existing cash of $155,492 and the $250k-$1m Elitesoft facility are insufficient alone for a genuine commercial scale-up). Modelled at $0.006/share -- double the current stale $0.003 print, reflecting the sentiment improvement a first signed contract would likely bring, but still a heavily dilutive raise given the tiny absolute dollar amount relative to the existing 514.9m share base.

bear.narrative: The controlling shareholder's support (a non-binding 12-month letter) is not renewed, or the Elitesoft Asia facility is not honoured/expanded, before any commercial breakthrough occurs -- consistent with 7+ years of zero revenue and now-permanently-waived licence performance targets. The company exhausts its $155,492 cash cushion (unaided runway ~7 months) and enters a wind-up. Even an ORDERLY wind-up consumes the remaining $53,803 of net assets in liquidator/wind-up costs (deregistration, final audit, professional fees, any residual lease/contract termination costs), leaving ordinary equity holders with nothing.
bear.burn_note: FY2027 burn continues at the admin-only run rate until support is withdrawn mid-year and wind-up is triggered; no further cash flows modelled post wind-up.

base.funding_source: Continued related-party support (Chang Ku Ee support letter, Elitesoft Asia facility), consistent with the FY2026 disclosed going-concern basis
base.note: Revenue and burn shown for transparency on the cost of persisting as a shell; per the base-case methodology this burn is funded externally and is a wash against the tangible-equity valuation, not a further deduction from it.

bull.note: Interim annual FCF is not separately modelled year-by-year; the bull IV is derived directly from a year-5 exit enterprise value (revenue x exit multiple), discounted back 5 years at 30% WACC, net of the modelled dilutive capital raise -- see assumptions.bull for the full build.

bear.note: Wind-up assumed to occur during/immediately after FY2027 once related-party support is withdrawn or not renewed.

base.methodology: intrinsic_value = (FY2026 shareholders' equity + shell scarcity value) / shares outstanding = (53,803 + 300,000) / 514,894,500 = NZ$0.0006871/share

bull.methodology: intrinsic_value = [year-5 exit EV (revenue $1.5m x 1.5x multiple = $2.25m), discounted 5 years at 30% WACC = $605,990] / [514.9m existing shares + 125.0m new shares from the modelled $750k dilutive raise = 639.9m shares] = NZ$0.0009470/share. Even this successful-commercialisation scenario, which assumes a first signed contract and a genuine (if still niche) $1.5m revenue run-rate by year 5, values the stock roughly 68% BELOW the current $0.003 stale quote.

bear.methodology: Direct insolvency/wind-up: even an orderly wind-up consumes the remaining $53,803 of net assets in liquidation/deregistration costs, once professional and closing-out fees are applied to a company with no saleable operating business and a single-licence intangible asset with no independently verified market value. Ordinary equity holders receive NZ$0.0000/share.

entry_price.not_meaningful_note: A standard 15%-IRR entry-price formula assumes a cash-generating asset whose interim distributions plus a fair-value exit can be discounted back to a purchase price. IPR generates no distributable cash flow (FCF has been negative in every year on record), pays no dividends, and its 'exit value' in every scenario is either zero (bear), a static book-value-plus-scarcity claim not expected to compound (base), or a discrete, already-heavily-discounted and already-diluted 5-year commercialisation outcome (bull). Consistent with the AFC.NZ/BGI.NZ precedent, this section treats the probability-weighted intrinsic value itself as a year-5 exit value with zero interim distributions, and discounts that back to today at the 15% hurdle -- i.e. it asks 'what price today, with no interim cash flow, compounds to the weighted fair value in 5 years at 15%/yr', which is the closest honest analogue to the standard formula for a non-cash-flowing shell.

base.interim_distributions_note: No dividends, buybacks, or other cash distributions have ever been made or are contemplated; going-concern burn is funded by/for the company, not distributed to shareholders, so interim cash flow to the equity holder is NIL under every scenario.
base.exit_equity_value_note: Base-case exit value assumed structurally similar to today (tangible equity + shell scarcity value); continued related-party funding is assumed to keep book equity roughly stable (external funding replaces burn), not to compound it.
base.weighted_exit_value_note: The probability-weighted intrinsic value (see probability_weighted.weighted_iv) x shares outstanding, used as the single 'exit value' input to the entry-price formula below, is more representative than the base case alone since it blends all three scenarios' likelihoods.
base.entry_price_methodology: entry_price = weighted_iv / (1 + hurdle_rate)^years = 0.0002587 / (1.15)^5 = NZ$0.0001286/share -- the price today that, with zero interim distributions, compounds to the probability-weighted fair value in 5 years at a 15% annual return.
base.untradeable_note: This computed entry price (NZ$0.0001286) sits well below the current NZ$0.003 stale quote and, in practice, below any price the market has shown willingness to trade at recently -- the stock has effectively not traded since October 2025. No price at which this stock could be bought today is consistent with a 15% IRR to the probability-weighted outcome; the only executable price is whatever a counterparty is willing to quote, which the last 10 months of zero volume suggests may not exist at all in practical size.

recommended_entry_price.note: For this non-cash-flowing, pre-revenue shell, the more decision-useful 'entry price' is simply the probability-weighted fair value itself (see probability_weighted.weighted_iv) -- the maximum price a rational buyer should pay given the scenario mix, since no compounding cash-flow mechanics apply in a way that makes a lower, IRR-adjusted number more meaningful than the fair value itself. Both this figure and the formal 15%-hurdle calculation above land on the same conclusion: the current $0.003 stale quote is priced far above any fundamentals-based scenario.

sensitivity.description: A standard WACC / terminal-growth grid is not meaningful here (no perpetuity cash-flow stream exists). Instead this matrix sensitizes the probability-WEIGHTED intrinsic value to (rows) the bear-case probability weight (with the residual split 80/20 base/bull) and (columns) the base-case NZX-listing scarcity value assumption -- the two inputs the valuation is most sensitive to.
sensitivity.matrix_read_note: Row = bear-case probability weight, from 50% (relatively optimistic given 7+ years of zero revenue and permanently-waived licence targets) to 80% (near-certainty of failure). Column = NZX shell/listing scarcity value from NZ$0 (no promoter interest at all) to NZ$600,000 (near the top of observed NZX shell-value precedent for a company of this size). Every single cell in this 5x5 grid is far below the current NZ$0.003 stale quote (which requires an implied equity value of ~NZ$1.54m -- roughly 4.4x the most generous NZ$0.0006026/share cell -- just to be fair value).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear is weighted heaviest (65%) given: (1) ZERO revenue in every year since inception of the licence, roughly 7 years running, with the original licence's own contractual performance targets (customer numbers, SGD$150,000 revenue by Sept-2026) and the inventor's royalty PERMANENTLY WAIVED post FY2026 year-end -- the closest counterparty to the technology no longer expects the originally-contracted commercial timeline to be met; (2) explicit auditor Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern; (3) unaided cash runway of only ~7 months ($155,492 cash / ~$270k annual burn) against total dependence on a single controlling shareholder's NON-BINDING 12-month support letter and a related-party facility from a company controlled by that same shareholder; (4) a negligible equity cushion (total equity $53,803, roughly 29% of total assets) that a single further loss-making year would likely erase even with continued support; and (5) near-zero free float (~14%) and no genuine trading since October 2025, meaning even a fundamentals-driven repricing lower would show little market confirmation either way. Base (28%) reflects that the controlling shareholder HAS, to date, consistently chosen to keep funding the shell (interest-free loans, the new Elitesoft facility, a fresh 12-month support commitment, and the outsourcing partner's fee waiver through FY2028), so continued life-support for another 1-3 years is a real possibility, not just a bear-case tail. Bull (7%) is kept deliberately small: unlike AFC.NZ's pre-MOU RTO discussion or BGI.NZ's shell-only optionality, IPR at least has a live, named-if-unnamed commercial trial (the multinational chocolate manufacturer's jute-bag pilot) rather than pure listing optionality -- but after 7+ years of trials without a single sale, and with the original licence targets just having been waived rather than met, a first genuine signed commercial agreement within the modelled 5-year horizon is a low-probability, not base-rate, outcome.

sanity_check.current_price_pe_note: P/E is undefined -- Iperion has never reported positive earnings (net loss every year FY2019-FY2026) and has zero revenue, so no earnings-based multiple can be constructed.
sanity_check.current_price_ev_ebitda_note: EV/EBITDA is undefined -- with zero revenue there is no EBITDA to speak of (operating loss every year, no gross profit line since there are no sales); an EBITDA-based multiple cannot be constructed for a pre-revenue company.
sanity_check.current_price_pb_note: At the current NZ$0.003 stale quote, market cap is ~NZ$1,544,684 against FY2026 shareholders' equity of NZ$53,803 -- an implied Price/Book of ~28.7x. Historical P/B computed from Yahoo monthly prices against each fiscal year-end's reported book value per share tells a very different story: FY2019 ~0.21x, FY2020 ~0.24x, FY2024 ~1.9x, FY2025 ~4.3x, FY2026 ~28.7x. The CURRENT 28.7x multiple is the extreme historical outlier, not the model -- it is a mechanical artifact of the share price being frozen (unchanged at $0.003 since December 2023, effectively untraded since October 2025) while reported book equity has collapsed roughly 85% since FY2024 alone (from $814,081 to $53,803) as accumulated losses consumed nearly all remaining issued capital. A stock cannot be said to be 'worth' 28.7x book when the numerator (price) has not moved for years while the denominator (book value) fell by nearly 15x over the same period -- that is a stale-price artifact, not a re-rating.
trip_reasons: Market price (NZ$0.003) has not moved materially since December 2023 (unchanged at exactly $0.003 in every monthly print) and shows no genuine trading since October 2025 -- it cannot reflect deteriorating FY2025/FY2026 fundamentals because there has been no price discovery to incorporate them.

Implied P/B of ~28.7x at the current quote is 6.7x-137x the historical P/B range observed FY2019-FY2025 (0.21x-4.3x), and far above what any of the three fundamentals-based scenarios modelled here support (bear 0x, base ~6.6x, bull ~9.1x book, all measured against FY2026 book value of $53,803).
All three scenario intrinsic values (NZ$0.0000, NZ$0.0006871, NZ$0.0009470) and the probability-weighted intrinsic value (NZ$0.0002587) sit far below the NZ$0.003 current price, by 68%-100%.

The company's own base-case going-concern forecast (disclosed in the FY2026 annual report) assumes ZERO sales for FY2027 -- i.e. management itself is not underwriting the near-term commercial breakthrough that would be needed to justify the current market cap on any operating basis.

The computed 15%-IRR entry price (NZ$0.0001286) and even the more generous probability-weighted fair value (NZ$0.0002587) both sit an order of magnitude below the current quote, meaning no price at which this stock could satisfy a normal return hurdle is reasonably close to being executable.
sanity_check.fix_applied: asset-based scenario valuation instead of growth DCF; P/E and EV/EBITDA reported as null (undefined for a zero-revenue, loss-making company) with P/B used as the sole historical multiple anchor

stacked_build.component: NZ small-cap base cost of equity
stacked_build.note: Baseline cost of equity for a small, illiquid NZX-listed company, before any company-specific risk loadings.
Market cap is only ~NZ$1.5m and the stock has shown effectively zero genuine trading volume since October 2025 -- a severe illiquidity discount is warranted beyond a normal small-cap premium.
Auditor Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph, ~7 months of unaided cash runway, and total dependence on a non-binding 12-month related-party support letter.

The entire equity value case rests on one licensed technology (Pathoglaze) with zero commercial sales in 7+ years and now-permanently-waived performance targets -- a binary, unproven commercialisation outcome.

77.4% controlling shareholder is simultaneously the primary funding source (directly and via the related Elitesoft Asia facility); minority shareholders (~14% free float) have negligible influence over financing terms, dilution, or strategic direction.

wacc_rationale.note: This 30% figure is used only for the entry-price 15%-hurdle discounting mechanics and the bull-case 5-year exit-value discounting -- it does NOT discount a perpetuity FCF stream, because none exists. A conventional 11-12% NZ WACC (appropriate for a going, cash-generating small-cap) would materially understate the risk profile of a pre-revenue, going-concern-qualified, single-product shell reliant on one controlling shareholder's discretionary support.

valuation_philosophy.why_not_a_gordon_growth_fcf_dcf: Iperion has never earned a dollar of revenue in any period on record (FY2019 through FY2026, audited). Every year's free cash flow is negative -- FY2026: -$269,849; FY2025: -$447,900; FY2024: -$734,204 -- with no positive year to anchor a base FCF, no growth rate to compound (there is nothing to grow FROM), and consequently no terminal value that can be meaningfully capitalised via Gordon growth. Attempting a conventional component-built or flat-margin FCF DCF here would either (a) extrapolate a structural, uninterrupted cash-burn machine into an increasingly negative and economically meaningless valuation, or (b) require fabricating a hypothetical future revenue/margin ramp dressed up as a 'DCF' when the honest position is that no such business yet exists -- which is precisely why this model instead uses an explicit, clearly-labelled scenario framework (bear/base/bull) where any assumed future revenue (in the bull case only) is presented as exactly what it is: an illustrative, heavily-discounted, heavily-diluted 'what does success look like' construction, not a DCF projection with false precision.
valuation_philosophy.going_concern: The FY2026 audited financial statements (signed 30-Jun-2026) contain an explicit Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph. Cash of $155,492 against an annual operating cash burn of $269,849 implies roughly 7 months of unaided runway. The company continues to operate only because (a) Three Summit Ventures, the outsourced manufacturing partner, has voluntarily waived its normally-fixed $400,000/year facility fee through 31-Mar-2028, and (b) the controlling shareholder, Chang Ku Ee (77.4%), has given a 12-month financial support commitment and made available a $250,000 facility (expandable to US$1,000,000 subject to approval) via the related Elitesoft Asia Sdn Bhd. Both lifelines are discretionary/non-binding beyond their stated terms and could be withdrawn or not renewed.
valuation_philosophy.value_rests_on_option_and_scarcity: To the extent this equity is worth anything above zero, that value rests on (a) a small NZX-listing scarcity premium (the base case), reflecting the modest demand for tiny, compliant NZX shells as reverse-listing vehicles, even absent any currently-disclosed RTO discussion (unlike AFC.NZ's pre-MOU status, IPR has no disclosed RTO counterparty at all -- this is pure listing optionality, not transaction-specific option value), and (b) speculative, heavily-discounted and heavily-diluted optionality on the Pathoglaze technology eventually converting its multi-year trial relationship with an unnamed multinational chocolate manufacturer into a first signed commercial agreement (the bull case). Neither is a claim on any existing or near-term cash-generating business -- the company's OWN base-case going-concern forecast for FY2027 assumes zero sales.
valuation_philosophy.weighted_iv_far_below_price: The probability-weighted intrinsic value across all three scenarios (NZ$0.0002587/share) sits roughly 91% below the current NZ$0.003 quote, and even the single most optimistic scenario modelled (a first signed commercial contract converting into a genuine, if still niche, $1.5m revenue run-rate by year 5, net of a heavily dilutive capital raise) remains roughly 68% below the current price. This is the correct, honest output of the model given the underlying facts -- market cap of ~NZ$1.5m sits at ~28.7x FY2026 net tangible assets of $53,803 for a company that has never sold a single unit of product, and the model is not adjusted to narrow that gap.
valuation_philosophy.uninvestable_conclusion: IPR.NZ is effectively uninvestable on a fundamentals basis at the current stale quote. The NZ$0.003 price has not moved since December 2023 and has shown no genuine trading since October 2025 -- it is a stale last-print sitting near the NZX tick floor, not a market-clearing valuation of the underlying (non-existent) business. Any perceived 'value' in owning IPR shares today is a small-dollar, binary, heavily-diluted bet on an unconfirmed, multi-year-running Pathoglaze commercialisation trial finally converting to a signed contract, layered on top of a going-concern shell that is entirely dependent on one controlling shareholder's discretionary support to survive to see that outcome.
